Before establishing the business, he worked across telecommunications, electronics and textiles, including management roles in family companies. A law graduate of Bahçeşehir University, he also practised as an attorney and later led Papara as chief executive.

long_biography.plain_text:
Turkish entrepreneur Ahmet Faruk Karslı began with a struggling mobile-phone dealership at seventeen. He brought it into profit within three months and sold the business two years later. That early experience preceded a succession of ventures in different industries before he entered financial services.

At Papara, Karslı favoured developing technology internally so the company could introduce services without depending on outside suppliers. He wanted customer communications to avoid banking jargon and explain products plainly. His pricing model charged the most intensive users while keeping ordinary services free for the majority. Staff feedback also shaped a hybrid working arrangement, alongside training and career development.
